title: Case 430

plan.situation: Order NCW-8841 (6 e-bike conversion kits, each with a lithium-ion battery, CAD 7,380.00, tracking TPC-4471-0098) is held by Arctic Meridian Airways' acceptance desk under AWB 417-30291846. The airline rejected the shipper's Dangerous Goods declaration, which had no UN number or proper shipping name, no net quantity, no Packing Instruction and no DG training reference for the signatory. Northfield's Gabe Lindqvist signed it, does not remember any DG training, and wants the desk to 'push the carrier'. The customer, Ellie Akpalialuk of Qaqqaq Outfitters, is asking for an update. She offers to take a partial delivery, or to have a local electrician do assembly if parts arrive by 14 February.

facts.fact: Tundra's status note says the shipment was handed to the airline for the air leg on 2026-01-30 16:55 CST, and has been DELAYED_AT_HUB since 2026-02-02

The airline did not accept the Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods it received 2026-01-31. Missing: UN number and proper shipping name, net quantity per package, Packing Instruction, and the signatory's DG training certificate reference. Pieces are held in the cargo shed and not manifested
Pieces are released after a corrected declaration passes the acceptance check. After acceptance, the next uplifts to Iqaluit are Thursday and Sunday
Storage is free for 5 days from receipt, then CAD 38.00 per day. Pieces not accepted within 10 days of receipt go back to origin at the shipper's cost
The airline notice went to Tundra's ops mailbox, ops@tundraparcel.example, with the desk copied
Tundra support said there was 'no exception on our side, depends on the airline, probably next flight'
Gabe signed the DG declaration, does not remember any DG training, says earlier battery shipments went as standard parcels, and asks the desk to 'just push the carrier'
The customer's tour season starts 20 Feb. A local electrician could take over assembly if parts arrive by 14 Feb. A partial delivery is acceptable
Every kit includes a lithium-ion battery, so any partial shipment would still be dangerous goods
The return-to-origin deadline is about 9 Feb (counting from the 30 Jan handover) or 10 Feb (counting from the 31 Jan declaration receipt)

conflicts: Tundra support (event 004) said there was no exception on the carrier side and it would 'probably' go on the next flight. The airline's acceptance desk (event 006) says the pieces are held on a rejected DG declaration and not manifested. Tundra ops should resolve this; the desk does not pick a side.
Gabe says everything was packed and labelled correctly (event 005), but the airline rejected the declaration on four specific points (event 006).
It is unclear whether 'receipt' for the storage and return clocks means 30 Jan or 31 Jan. Only the airline or Tundra can confirm this.
missing_information: Whether Northfield has, or can get, a DG-trained preparer for a corrected declaration
Tundra's route and contact for resubmitting the corrected declaration, and whether Tundra offers DG preparation
The exact receipt date that starts the storage and return-to-origin clocks
Whether the consignment can be split
Who pays any storage after the free period
risk_flags: Safety and regulatory: lithium-ion batteries were offered for air transport under a non-compliant DG declaration. Only a DG-trained preparer and the airline decide. The desk gives no DG content advice.
'Push the carrier' would mean pressing for uplift without DG acceptance. Declined.
Earlier battery shipments reportedly went as standard parcels. That is a possible undeclared-DG matter for the carrier and merchant to review. The desk accuses no one.
Deadline: the pieces go back to origin around 9-10 Feb if not accepted. The customer's dates are 14 and 20 Feb.
Money: storage at CAD 38.00 per day after the free period, and a return at the shipper's cost. Only recorded amounts are quoted.
Privacy: Gabe's training status and internal details are not shared with the customer.

authority_map.controls: Issuing a corrected DG declaration signed by a DG-trained person; reship or split decisions

authority_map.party: Arctic Meridian Airways Cargo Terminal Winnipeg, acceptance desk
authority_map.controls: DG acceptance, uplift, storage charges, return to origin
The AWB with the airline, the resubmission route, the carrier-side record
Accepting a partial delivery and arranging local assembly
Coordination only. No authority to push uplift, fill in DG content, or commit to charges or dates

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: The desk has made no promise to the customer. New since her first message: the airline's DG rejection (event 006), Gabe's statement about training (event 007), and her partial-delivery and assembly offer (event 008)

plan.decision_summary: Ask Northfield to have a DG-trained person issue a corrected Dangerous Goods declaration and send it through Tundra for AWB 417-30291846 before the return-to-origin deadline. Decline to 'push' uplift, and give the customer an honest update with no arrival date. Both messages wait for human approval (hard gate, DG/safety).
plan.rationale: The airline's DG acceptance is the only blocker, and only the shipper, through a trained signatory, can fix the declaration. Pushing for uplift would be unsafe and cannot work. The customer asked twice and has hard dates, so she should get the true reason now, with no unconfirmed ETA. The two-message limit is used for the owner request and the requester update. The previous draft told Gabe that the desk was asking Tundra to confirm the return date, but no message to Tundra was planned. That sentence is removed. Gabe, as shipper, is asked to confirm the resubmission route and the clock date with Tundra. The questions for Tundra ops are recorded as the desk's next carrier step, and nothing claims a message already sent.

actions.subject: NCW-8841 / AWB 417-30291846 - airline has rejected the Dangerous Goods declaration; corrected declaration needed
actions.purpose: Ask the shipper to have a DG-trained person issue a corrected declaration, the only way to release the pieces
actions.body:
Hello Gabe,

This is about order NCW-8841 (tracking TPC-4471-0098, air waybill 417-30291846). On 2026-02-03 at 16:08 CST, the Arctic Meridian Airways Cargo Terminal Winnipeg acceptance desk said it had not accepted the Shipper's Declaration for Dangerous Goods it received on 2026-01-31. Its findings were:
- no UN number or proper shipping name for the lithium-ion batteries packed with equipment
- net quantity per package missing
- Packing Instruction reference missing
- no DG training certificate reference for the signatory

The pieces are in the airline's cargo shed and are not on a flight manifest. The airline will release them only after a corrected declaration passes its acceptance check. Neither Tundra nor this desk can override that, so we cannot push the carrier to load them.

What we need from you:
1. Please have a corrected declaration prepared and signed by a person with current dangerous-goods training (your own staff or a qualified DG preparation service), and submit it through Tundra Parcel Co for AWB 417-30291846. Please don't sign it yourself unless you hold that training. We can't advise on what the declaration should contain; that must come from the trained preparer.
2. As the shipper, please confirm with Tundra Parcel Co how to resubmit, and the exact date the airline's storage and return clocks started.

Please reply by 12:00 CST on 2026-02-04 with who will prepare the declaration and when you expect to submit it.

Timing, as the airline stated it:
- After acceptance, the next flights to Iqaluit are on Thursday and Sunday.
- Storage is free for 5 days from receipt, then CAD 38.00 per day.
- Pieces not accepted within 10 days of receipt go back to origin at the shipper's cost. By our reading that is around 9-10 February, but the airline has not confirmed the exact date.

This is a request, not a confirmation of any release or flight.

Tamsin Okafor
Prairie Relay Order Desk

actions.subject: Order NCW-8841 - why your kits are held
actions.purpose: Give the customer an honest status update without promising an arrival date, and ask her to tell us if her dates change
actions.body:
Hello Ellie,

Thanks for your messages. Here is where order NCW-8841 (tracking TPC-4471-0098) stands. The kits are being held at the airline's cargo terminal in Winnipeg. The airline needs corrected dangerous-goods shipping paperwork for the lithium-ion batteries in the kits. That paperwork has to come from the sender, Northfield Cycle Works, and we have asked them to provide it urgently.

Once the airline accepts the corrected paperwork, its next flights to Iqaluit run on Thursdays and Sundays. We can't give you an arrival date yet, because we don't know when the paperwork will be accepted.

Thank you for offering to take a partial delivery and to arrange local assembly. Every kit includes a battery, so sending some kits early would still need the same paperwork check. We have your 14 February assembly date and your 20 February season start on record. If either date changes, please let us know here.

We'll update you here as soon as the sender or the airline confirms the next step.

Tamsin Okafor
Prairie Relay Order Desk

actions.purpose: Record the real cause, the conflict, and the open questions for Tundra ops as the next carrier step
actions.body: The hold is caused by the airline's DG rejection (event 006), not 'delay at hub'. This conflicts with Tundra support's 'no exception' (event 004). Next step: email Tundra Parcel Co ops (ops@tundraparcel.example) about AWB 417-30291846 / TPC-4471-0098, noting the conflict with event 004. Ask Tundra ops to confirm: (1) the receipt date that starts the 5-day storage and 10-day return clocks (30 vs 31 Jan); (2) the resubmission route and contact for a corrected DG declaration, and whether Tundra offers DG preparation; (3) whether the consignment can be split. Also refer the earlier battery shipments Gabe says went as standard parcels to Tundra's DG/safety team for review, with no accusation made. Gabe's request to 'push the carrier' was declined. Both outbound messages are held for human approval (hard gate).

actions.purpose: Check Northfield's reply at the time given in the request
actions.body: Check whether Northfield named a DG-trained preparer and a submission time for AWB 417-30291846, and whether Tundra confirmed the clock date. If not, escalate to the supervisor, because the pieces go back to origin around 9-10 Feb and the Thursday 5 Feb flight is at risk.

not_doing: Not pressing Tundra or the airline to load the batteries without DG acceptance. That is unsafe and outside anyone's authority.
Not advising on UN numbers, packing instructions or how to fill in the declaration. That is for a DG-trained preparer only.
Not promising the customer an arrival date or arrival by 14 or 20 Feb, and not suggesting partial delivery avoids the check.
Not telling Gabe that the desk has already asked Tundra for anything. Tundra is not contacted in this step because of the two-message limit; its questions are recorded as the next step.
Not telling the customer about Gabe's training status or internal details.
Not quoting a total storage charge or deciding who pays.
Not saying the kits are 'safe'. The record only says they are held.
Not accusing anyone over the earlier standard-parcel shipments.
plan.follow_up: At 12:00 CST on 2026-02-04, check for Northfield's confirmation of a DG-trained preparer and a submission time. Then email Tundra ops with the questions in the case note. If Northfield is silent, escalate to the supervisor before the Thursday 5 Feb flight. Only an airline acceptance notice, followed by a manifest/uplift scan, counts as release. Update Ellie when either happens.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Ask Northfield Cycle Works to get a corrected Dangerous Goods declaration issued and signed by a DG-trained person and resubmitted through Tundra for AWB 417-30291846 before the return-to-origin deadline. Decline to 'push' uplift, and give the customer an honest update with no arrival date. Both messages wait for human approval because this is a safety/DG matter.

issues.problem: The email to Gabe says 'we are asking Tundra to confirm the exact date', but no action in the plan contacts Tundra ops. Their questions only go into an internal case note (action 2). So the message describes a step the desk has not planned to take. Tundra also controls the resubmission route for the AWB, and Gabe is being told to send the corrected declaration that way, yet Tundra is never asked about it.
issues.fix: Add a send_message to Tundra Parcel Co ops (ops@tundraparcel.example, the carrier's operations mailbox in the record) for AWB 417-30291846 / TPC-4471-0098. Ask them to confirm three things: the receipt date that starts the 5-day storage clock and the 10-day return clock (30 vs 31 Jan); the route and contact for resubmitting a corrected DG declaration, and whether they offer DG preparation; and whether the consignment can be split. Note the conflict with what their support line said in event 004. If you don't add this, take the 'we are asking Tundra' sentence out of Gabe's email.

issues.problem: 'The kits are safe at the airline's cargo terminal' goes slightly beyond the record, which only says the pieces are 'held in the cargo shed'. The action_class is ask_customer, but the message asks her nothing. The 'Customer portal' channel is not in the record; she wrote in through the web form.
issues.fix: Say 'held at the airline's cargo terminal'. Change the action_class to an update or inform class. Reply through the same web form or ticket channel she used.

issues.problem: requester_type is set to 'consumer', but Qaqqaq Outfitters is a small business.
issues.fix: Set requester_type to business or small_business.

review.summary: The plan is sound overall: it correctly finds the airline's DG rejection as the blocker, asks the shipper for a declaration from a trained preparer, declines to 'push' the carrier, avoids giving DG advice or an ETA, and holds both messages for human approval. But Gabe's email says the desk is asking Tundra to confirm the return date, and no action actually contacts Tundra ops. Add that message (or remove the claim) and fix the minor wording and channel points.

review_rounds.plan_summary: Ask Northfield to have a DG-trained person issue a corrected Dangerous Goods declaration and send it through Tundra for AWB 417-30291846 before the return-to-origin deadline. Decline to 'push' uplift, and give the customer an honest update with no arrival date. Both messages wait for human approval (hard gate, DG/safety).

issues.problem: The airline said the next uplifts after acceptance are 'Thursday and Sunday'. The customer message turns this into a standing schedule ('run on Thursdays and Sundays'), which the record does not say.
issues.fix: Change it to 'the airline's next flights to Iqaluit after acceptance are on Thursday and Sunday'. Or add that later dates have not been confirmed.

issues.problem: The message tells Ellie 'we have asked them to provide it urgently', but the request to Northfield is waiting for approval in the same batch and has not been sent yet.
issues.fix: Make sure the Northfield email goes out before or at the same time as the customer update.

review.summary: The plan sends the corrected-declaration request to the shipper, who controls the fix. It refuses to push for loading without dangerous-goods acceptance, gives the customer an honest update with no arrival date and none of the shipper's internal details, and quotes only amounts and dates from the record, with the return deadline worked out correctly and hedged. Both messages wait for human approval, and the questions for Tundra are recorded as the next step without claiming they were sent. There are only two small wording and ordering points.
